payload.name: Preserve candidate facts during memory merge
payload.description: When merging a memory candidate into an existing memory, use this if the candidate contains a fact absent from the target; ensure the merged version retains the candidate's full set of facts, including ongoing plans.
content: Before MERGE, compare the candidate content against the target memory content. Any discrete fact present in the candidate but not in the target must appear in the merged content, even if the target is an event and the candidate is a plan.

When the candidate's memory kind differs from the target's (e.g., merging a plan into an event), treat the candidate's predicate as a durable fact that must survive the merge; do not replace content with a summary that omits it.

candidates.solves: Construction decisions sometimes merge a candidate into an existing memory and the merged text drops facts that were only in the candidate, especially when the candidate is a different memory kind (e.g., a plan) and the target is an event. This leads to unsupported future answers. The rule applies to any future merge where candidate and target overlap topically but the candidate introduces a new predicate, such as an ongoing donation, commitment, or other persistent fact; the merged memory must preserve that fact explicitly.

payload.name: Preserve Past Event Facts During Update
payload.description: When updating an existing past event memory and the new message introduces a future plan or separate event involving the same subject, use ADD for the new plan/event and do not change the existing memory's kind, world_start, or original content.
content: Before UPDATE, check whether the incoming information describes a different time period or event kind than the existing memory's stored timeframe. If so, do not overwrite the existing event's memory_kind, world_start/world_end, or core facts; create a new memory instead.

When a message mentions a future plan (e.g., 'next month') and the retrieved memory is a completed past event, keep the past event unchanged and ADD a separate `plan` memory for the future item with its own date.

If an UPDATE is genuinely enriching the same event, preserve the original event's date and memory_kind and only append compatible details; never promote an event to a plan or shift its start date to match a new plan.

candidates.solves: Construction updates often corrupt correct past-event memories when later messages introduce a related future plan or separate event. This Skill ensures distinct facts are kept as distinct memories, preventing loss of date ranges and event kind, and applies to any subject where a future plan or separate event is mentioned after a past event has been stored.

payload.name: Preserve original event facts on related updates
payload.description: When updating an existing event memory and the incoming message describes a later development of the same project, work, or task, preserve the original achievement facts by adding a new memory or limiting the update to changed fields.
content: If a new message reports a later development of an already recorded event (e.g., showing, publishing, or presenting completed work), do not replace the original event content with the new development.
Prefer ADD a separate event memory for the later development, or UPDATE only non-core fields while retaining the original completion date, action, and outcome.
During extraction, when the same subject/work appears in a later message, extract the new information as a candidate for a new event unless the message explicitly revises the earlier fact.

candidates.solves: When a later message describes a new development of a work whose original completion was already stored, the construction agent sometimes overwrites the older event memory, erasing original achievement facts. The reusable rule is to treat later related developments as additive or separate memories, preserving completion and date. This applies whenever a new message references a previously recorded project, task, or creation.

payload.name: Maintain cumulative counts for repeated events
payload.description: Apply when extracting or updating memories and a new message describes another occurrence of an event type already recorded for the same subject, especially wording like 'another', 'again', or 'second time'; use it to store the cumulative occurrence count.
content: When a message describes another occurrence of a countable event already recorded for the same subject, extract a memory that states the cumulative total (e.g., 'second rejection', 'two rejections') rather than only recording the new isolated instance.

Before ADDing a repeated event, search the existing memory pool for prior events of the same subject and event type; if found, create or update an aggregate memory with the total count and mention the prior occurrence dates, while keeping individual event memories intact.

candidates.solves: The construction agent stored each repeated rejection as an isolated event without an explicit total, so a later question asking how many times the event occurred could not be answered from memory. The reusable mechanism is that repeated countable events for the same subject need an explicit cumulative count maintained as new occurrences arrive, not just separate event records. This applies to any future conversation where the same type of countable event recurs (rejections, wins, submissions, purchases) and a count query may follow.

payload.name: Preserve-all-explicitly-enumerated-components
payload.description: When extracting or updating memory from a message that explicitly lists multiple distinct qualities, reasons, or preferences, use this to ensure every listed component is preserved and none is omitted during summarization.
content: During extraction, if the source message explicitly enumerates multiple distinct traits, reasons, or preferences, write the candidate to include every enumerated component; do not condense by dropping any item.

Before committing a memory, compare its content against the source message's list and verify that each explicitly stated component is represented, adding any missing item to the memory content or update.

candidates.solves: Lossy paraphrasing during extraction omits one component when a source explicitly lists multiple qualities. A preserve-every-listed-item rule fixes this and applies to any future multi-item preference, reason, or attribute statement, without inventing unstated details.

payload.name: Cross-check multi-message candidates for explicit facts
payload.description: When extracting a memory candidate from multiple messages that describe the same event, verify that all explicit factual statements from each source message are included in the candidate before finalizing.
content: When extracting a memory candidate from multiple messages, after drafting the candidate, re-read each source message and confirm that every explicit fact (activities, dates, locations, preferences, outcomes) is represented. If a fact is missing, add it to the candidate before emitting it.

candidates.solves: A memory candidate built from multiple messages about one event omitted an explicit activity from a later source message, causing incomplete memories. The rule is to verify each candidate against all source messages and include every explicit fact. It applies whenever extraction merges multiple messages into one candidate, across any topic such as trips or projects.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Object Descriptions as Candidates
payload.description: When a message contains a speaker describing an item they have, are showing, or own, extract a memory candidate for that object and its stated attributes during candidate extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, if a statement identifies an item (e.g., 'It's a map of...', 'I have a...', 'This is my...') and gives its type or attributes, generate a candidate memory capturing the item and those attributes.
Do not require the word 'favorite', 'love', or an explicit preference; an item's identity and description are memory-worthy facts.
Keep the candidate grounded in the exact stated attributes; do not infer additional traits beyond the message.

candidates.solves: The construction pipeline omitted an explicit fact because the message phrased it as a description of an item ('It's a map of...') rather than as a stated preference or plan, and no candidate was generated. Future sessions need a rule that during extraction, any utterance identifying an object the speaker possesses, shows, or references should produce a compact memory candidate for that object and its stated attributes, independent of the surface topic.

payload.name: PreserveAllStatedFactsWhenExtractingActivityDetails
payload.description: When extracting memory candidates from a message that describes an activity with multiple distinct facets, or before accepting an UPDATE/MERGE that enriches an event memory, use all stated facts from the source and drop none.
content: During extraction, if a message describes an activity with several distinct facts (e.g., what the subject does, what companions or pets do, outcomes, social benefits), include every stated fact in the candidate content; do not omit a fact because it is tangential to the existing memory's current focus.

Before accepting an UPDATE or MERGE, compare the proposed new memory content against the source message; if any stated fact from the source is absent from both the candidate and the existing memory, add it to the candidate or create a separate candidate so the memory remains complete.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates that describe a recurring activity sometimes keep only the facts aligned with the existing memory's topic and drop other stated details, leaving memories incomplete. This rule applies when a message lists multiple distinct facets of one activity (what the subject does, what companions or pets do, social outcomes) and requires preserving every independent fact in extraction and in later UPDATE/MERGE verification. It does not require adding unstated inferences or merging unrelated topics.

payload.name: Preserve All Explicit Actions During Extraction
payload.description: When a user message lists multiple concrete actions taken in response to an event, use during extraction and updates to ensure every explicit action is captured in memory rather than replaced by a general summary.
content: During candidate extraction, when a message describes a sequence of concrete actions taken by a person, preserve every discrete action in the extracted memory content; do not replace the action list with only an inferred general relationship, feeling, or attribute.

During update or merge, before modifying an existing memory, check the source message for explicitly stated actions; if any action is missing from the current memory content, add those missing concrete details to the updated version rather than only enriching with broader inferences.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that candidate extraction omitted all four concrete calming actions from a message and kept only the inferred bond statement, so later recall of those actions failed. The reusable mechanism is extracting a general relational summary instead of preserving explicitly enumerated actions. This applies to any future conversation where a speaker lists multiple discrete actions in response to an event; memory must retain every stated action to answer 'how' questions.

payload.name: Preserve explicit categories over examples
payload.description: When extracting memory candidates from statements that name broad categories followed by examples, use this to keep the explicit high-level wording instead of only concrete examples.
content: During candidate extraction, when a statement names a high-level category, goal, or interest and then gives concrete examples, preserve the explicit high-level wording in the candidate; do not replace it with only the examples.
If a statement includes both a general category and examples, include both when possible; if only one fits, keep the general category because future questions may target it.

After drafting a candidate, compare it with the source message for any explicitly stated abstract terms; if they are missing and only examples remain, revise the candidate to retain the abstract terms.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is extraction summarization that dropped a speaker's explicitly stated category and kept only concrete examples, so the memory could not answer a later question about the category. This occurs whenever a speaker names a broad category or goal and then illustrates it with examples; the extractor keeps examples but drops the category. The rule applies to future construction extraction across topics, not to retrieval-side or memory-kind decisions.

payload.name: Extract per-entity attributes from multi-entity lists
payload.description: When a user message assigns distinct attributes to multiple identified entities (e.g., each pet's personality, each family member's trait), extract one memory candidate per entity during construction.
content: During extraction, if a user message assigns distinct attributes to multiple identified entities (named, ordinal, or otherwise), create one candidate for each entity-attribute pair; do not skip the message or collapse the list into a single aggregate candidate.
Include the entity descriptor (e.g., oldest, second, name) and the specific attribute in the candidate text, and bind it to the source message so each fact is independently retrievable.
Apply this rule to any entity type (pets, people, groups) and use an existing memory kind that fits the stable attribute; do not invent new memory kinds.

candidates.solves: The Construction Agent sometimes ingests a user message listing separate attributes for multiple entities (e.g., each pet's personality) but produces no extraction candidates, losing all listed facts. This rule directs extraction to split such multi-entity attribute lists into per-entity candidates so each fact is independently recallable. It applies whenever a speaker assigns distinct characteristics to each member of a group, but not when the message describes the group as a whole.

payload.name: Preserve concrete item type for product lines
payload.description: When extracting memories about a limited edition line, collection, or series, if the message explicitly names an example item type, preserve that type instead of only recording the generic 'line'.
content: During extraction, when a speaker introduces a product or creative work by pointing to a concrete example item and then says it belongs to a limited line, collection, or series, record the concrete item type as the object of the memory (e.g., 'made limited-edition hoodies'), not just 'made a limited edition line'.
When the concrete item noun appears earlier in the same message or nearby turns and is clearly the referent of the line/collection, use that noun even if the later sentence only says 'line'.

candidates.solves: Extraction often condenses a described line or collection to a generic label and drops the concrete item type the speaker explicitly attached to it (e.g., 'this hoodie ... limited edition line' loses 'hoodie'). This rule instructs extractors to preserve the specific noun in memory so future questions about what was made can be answered. It applies whenever a message ties a named example item to a broader series, but not when the item type is hypothetical or not explicitly identified.

payload.name: CaptureAllEnumeratedItems
payload.description: When a user message lists multiple distinct items, extract and retain every item in memory content; do not omit any when summarizing or updating.
content: During extraction, if a message enumerates two or more distinct items (e.g., separated by commas, conjunctions, or bullet points), include each item explicitly in the candidate content. Avoid summaries that may drop list elements; paraphrase minimally and keep all listed specifics.

During CRUD, compare new evidence against existing memories: if an item from an enumerated list is missing from the stored memory, update or merge to add that item rather than leaving the memory incomplete.

candidates.solves: Memory construction often loses details when a speaker enumerates multiple distinct items in one message; the resulting memory is incomplete and fails to support claims about dropped elements. This skill ensures extraction and CRUD preserve every explicitly listed item, so future questions about any element can be answered. It applies to any topic where a user lists multiple attributes, reasons, preferences, or experiences.

payload.name: Preserve enumerated specifics in extraction
payload.description: When a message lists multiple distinct actions, behaviors, or reasons connected by 'and' or commas, apply this before creating or updating a candidate memory to avoid collapsing them into one umbrella term.
content: Before writing a candidate from raw evidence, identify every distinct action, behavior, or mechanism the speaker lists (e.g., 'help and push each other').
Preserve each listed specific in the memory content, using close paraphrase; do not replace the whole list with a broader term like 'support' that omits one component.
If updating an existing memory, merge all enumerated specifics from the new evidence into the updated content rather than keeping only the first or most salient one.

candidates.solves: During extraction, a candidate paraphrased 'help and push each other' as 'support each other', dropping the specific 'push' component, so the memory only partially supported the reference claim. The failure mechanism is over-abstraction of conjunctive specifics in raw evidence. This rule applies whenever future messages enumerate multiple distinct actions, benefits, or reasons and the extraction step must retain each component to answer targeted questions.

payload.name: Extract enumerated recommended items
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists items one person recommends, provides, or selects for another, include the concrete items in the extracted memory instead of summarizing them as 'supplies' or 'help.'
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly enumerates specific items they recommend, provide, or choose for someone, record each concrete item in the candidate content; do not replace the list with a generic phrase like 'recommended supplies' or 'offered to help.'
When updating an existing memory, preserve and add the explicit item details from the current message; avoid summarization that drops named objects needed to answer future questions.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often summarizes that someone recommended or offered help while dropping the concrete items named in the message. This causes later questions about the specific recommended items to be unsupported. This skill applies whenever a message enumerates tangible items (supplies, tools, ingredients, equipment, etc.) in a recommendation, offer, plan, or transfer; future sessions asking what was recommended or needed should retrieve an itemized memory.

payload.name: Preserve-specific-recommendations-in-extraction
payload.description: During construction extraction, when a message contains specific advice, substitutions, or named recommendations, ensure the memory stores the concrete details rather than only a generic summary of interest or assistance.
content: When extracting from a message that names specific suggestions, substitutions, or tips, encode those concrete details in the memory content; do not reduce the message to a general statement about interest, help, or participation.
If a candidate only summarizes the speaker's general attitude but omits named items, revise it to include the factual recommendation before marking it ADD or UPDATE.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes summarize a speaker's general interest or offer of help while omitting the concrete substitutions or recommendations in the same message, leaving future questions about those specifics unanswerable. This Skill applies whenever a source message contains named advice, substitutions, or tips: the extracted memory must preserve those concrete facts instead of only the generic intent. It does not apply to messages containing only general statements with no specific recommendation.

payload.name: CaptureAllListedOptionsInMemory
payload.description: When a source message lists multiple options or alternatives (e.g., 'or', 'and', comma-separated), apply during extraction to keep all listed items in memory; do not drop items because later dialogue focuses on one.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source message explicitly enumerates two or more options/items (using 'or', 'and', commas, or slashes), include every enumerated item in the extracted memory content; do not omit one just because later messages elaborate only another.

When preparing an ADD or UPDATE, compare the proposed memory with its source evidence: if the evidence lists multiple distinct items, ensure each appears in the memory (or in another linked memory); if an existing memory omits an item from the same source, update it to add the missing item.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates often drop one alternative from a source message when later conversation focuses on another, leaving memory incomplete. This skill enforces completeness for explicitly enumerated options/lists in a single message, across topics. It applies during extraction and CRUD whenever a statement lists multiple items; it does not apply to single-item statements or to inferences beyond the evidence.

payload.name: Maintain-explicit-aggregate-counts-for-recurring-acquisitions
payload.description: When a conversation reveals multiple items in the same countable category for one person across separate messages, create or update an explicit total-count state memory during extraction and CRUD, not only individual event memories.
content: During extraction and CRUD, when a message adds a new item to a countable set already present in memory (e.g., pet, child, vehicle, book), also create or update a `state` memory for the owner that explicitly states the cumulative total (e.g., 'X has N pets').

Before writing the aggregate state, count all distinct items for that owner and category using existing memories plus the current message; do not rely on implication or leave the total for a future question to infer.
If an aggregate state memory already exists, UPDATE it with the new total and timestamp of the latest evidence; if none exists, ADD one. Preserve the individual item memories for traceability.

candidates.solves: Construction logged each added item (pet, child, vehicle, book) as an event but never saved an explicit cumulative count, so 'how many' questions were only partially answered. The failure is omitting an aggregate count when the same countable category grows across messages. Apply to any future multi-message accumulation of countable items for one owner; not to single one-off item mentions.

payload.name: Preserve explicit enumerations during extraction
payload.description: When extracting a memory candidate from a message that lists multiple distinct aspects, reasons, or outcomes, preserve all listed items in the memory content.
content: During candidate extraction, if source text explicitly lists multiple distinct qualities, reasons, outcomes, or preferences, include every listed item in the memory content. Do not silently drop any item while paraphrasing; if compressing, use a phrase that still covers all enumerated details.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction can drop items when paraphrasing an explicit enumeration, causing partial memory coverage. This skill applies when a source message lists multiple distinct qualities, reasons, outcomes, or preferences and a candidate memory is being created; it does not apply to inferred conclusions or to compressing redundant restatements. Preserving all listed items keeps future answers complete.

payload.name: PreserveObjectOfCreationEvents
payload.description: When a message says a person made/created/produced a named thing, include that object in the extracted memory before ADD or UPDATE.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source describes someone making/creating/producing something (including a line, collection, edition, or item), the extracted memory must state the explicit object; do not summarize the action alone.
Before ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, check that any direct object of a creation verb from the source appears in the candidate or target memory; if missing, include it.
Do not invent an object that is not present in the evidence.

candidates.solves: During extraction, the direct object of creation verbs like 'made' or 'created' is sometimes dropped, leaving a memory that records the action but not what was produced. This makes future questions like 'made what?' unanswerable. The rule requires preserving any explicitly named object of a creation/production event. It applies to messages describing someone making, designing, or producing a concrete thing, and does not apply when the source itself does not name an object.
